candidate.title: Sequencing by Synthesis
candidate.scope: The single Illumina poster footer schematic titled Sequencing by Synthesis: capture of an already adapter-bearing DNA strand on an oligo-bearing flowcell, bridge amplification, selective strand removal, Read 1, Index 1, P5-mediated turnaround with Index 2, and Read 2. This is the depicted indexed paired-end sequencing component, not a standalone biological sample-preparation assay or a claim that every Illumina platform/version uses this route. Bridge amplification and the named read/index steps are internal components, not additional target methods. The library represents DNA insert sequence through surface-attached complementary copies; its original biological target and preparation are not supplied. The flowcell icon and enlarged nucleotide/strand insets explain attachment and cyclic readout, rather than additional workflow branches. Source labels distinguish attachment, P5 deblocking, cleavage, and departing read products, but do not specify terminal 5-prime/3-prime groups, dye structures or cycling-reset chemistry. No primary papers are supplied or required; the catalogue supplies only the title, and no historical or primary-paper mechanistic claim is made.

operations.label: Adapter hybridizes to flowcell
operations.description: An adapter segment of the entering DNA strand base-pairs with a complementary short oligo fixed to the flowcell. The strand changes from an entering library molecule to a surface-hybridized template.
operations.mechanism: Adapter-to-surface-oligo hybridization; no covalent attachment of the entering strand is asserted.
operations.information_effect: The DNA insert is retained in a surface-addressable template molecule; capture does not introduce a new biological target.

evidence.locator: Left, Adapter hybridizes to flowcell: single long blue strand with differently colored terminal segments, short orange and green oligos fixed to the pale surface, and adapter-to-oligo pairing

operations.label: Reverse strand synthesis
operations.description: The surface oligo is extended along the captured forward library strand to make a complementary reverse strand. The output is a duplex containing the original forward strand and a newly synthesized surface-attached copy.
operations.mechanism: Primer extension is indicated by the upward arrow and the new paired strand; no enzyme identity is supplied.
operations.information_effect: The insert sequence is carried into a complementary DNA copy anchored through the surface primer.

evidence.locator: Left, Reverse strand synthesis: upward extension arrow beside surface primer; adjacent duplex labeled Forward strand and Reverse strand

operations.label: Remove forward strand
operations.description: Remove the original forward strand from the initial duplex, leaving its newly synthesized reverse complement attached to the flowcell. The faded departing strand is represented separately from the retained template.
operations.information_effect: The original strand leaves, while its sequence information persists in the surface-associated complement.

evidence.locator: Left, Remove forward strand: faded departing forward strand and retained full-length surface-attached reverse strand

operations.label: Fold over and hybridize to second primer
operations.description: The retained reverse strand bends toward the other surface primer and hybridizes through its available adapter region. It changes from a single attached straight template into a bridge held at the original anchor and the newly paired primer.
operations.mechanism: Intramolecular bending of the attached template and adapter-to-primer pairing at the surface; no mixing of separate library molecules is depicted.

evidence.locator: Left, Fold over and hybridize to second primer: single strand curved between its surface anchor and the other short surface primer

operations.label: Synthesize second strand
operations.description: Extend the second surface primer along the folded reverse template. A new complementary strand converts the initially single-stranded arch into a double-stranded bridge with the strands attached at opposite surface ends.
operations.information_effect: A second attached DNA copy carries the corresponding complementary insert information.

evidence.locator: Left, Synthesize second strand immediately before Bridge amplification: double-stranded arch with both primer-associated ends at the surface

operations.label: Bridge amplification; Thousands of molecules are amplified in parallel
operations.description: The curved arrows connect separated attached forward/reverse strands with newly synthesized double-stranded bridges. Repeated strand separation, folding to available surface primers and complementary synthesis expand the attached DNA population; the enlarged drawing depicts many molecules amplified in parallel.
operations.mechanism: The loop depicts repeated bridge formation and synthesis with separation into attached single strands, rather than a one-way transfer into a pooled solution.
operations.information_effect: The original library sequences are propagated as surface-associated copies that provide amplified sequencing templates. No quantitative relation to biological abundance is specified.

evidence.locator: Left-to-center, Bridge amplification: opposed curved arrows connect separate Forward strand/Reverse strand templates and two double-stranded bridges; enlarged group captioned Thousands of molecules are amplified in parallel

operations.label: The reverse strand is cleaved and washed away
operations.description: Selectively cleave and remove the amplified reverse strands. Retained full-length forward-orientation templates, together with short surface oligos/remnants, replace the mixed amplified population as the read-ready material.
operations.mechanism: Selective strand cleavage and removal are explicitly captioned; the cleavage site and chemistry are not specified.
operations.information_effect: The sequencing substrate is oriented to the retained template strand; this is strand selection, not biological target enrichment.

evidence.locator: Center, The reverse strand is cleaved and washed away: faded departing strand, short residual surface oligo, and full-length retained opposite strand

operations.label: Sequence primer; With each cycle, four fluorescently tagged nucleotides compete for addition to the growing chain
operations.description: The labeled sequence primer initiates a complementary read strand on the retained forward template. In each depicted cycle, the template determines which one of four fluorescently tagged nucleotides is incorporated. The growing read product and an ordered fluorescent readout result.
operations.mechanism: The source states that only one nucleotide is incorporated based on the template sequence and depicts successive colored signals. Fluorescent-signal reset chemistry is not illustrated.
operations.information_effect: The physical readout carrier is the primer-derived DNA extension on an amplified surface template; the ordered fluorescence identifies bases in the first read region. It measures the library DNA sequence, whose upstream biological provenance is unspecified.

evidence.locator: Center, Sequence primer and enlarged fluorescent incorporation series; caption With each cycle, four fluorescently tagged nucleotides compete for addition to the growing chain. Only one is incorporated based on the sequence of the template.

operations.label: The read product is washed away

operations.information_effect: The physical Read 1 extension is removed; the recorded Read 1 information and its template association are not a transferred DNA reagent.

operations.label: The read product is washed away

operations.label: Fold over and hybridize to first primer

operations.label: Deblock P5 primer and add unlabeled bases

operations.label: Sequence Index2
operations.description: Continue sequencing from the P5-derived extension on the folded template using the depicted fluorescent nucleotides. The complementary strand acquires an Index 2 read segment and remains attached for subsequent completion of the second strand.
operations.mechanism: The Index 2 drawing shows fluorescent incorporation on the complementary arm of the P5-extended bridge; it does not depict a separate soluble Index 2 primer or removal of this extension.
operations.information_effect: This index read shares the retained library template association with Read 1 and Index 1. Its preparation history is specific to the drawn P5 turnaround route.

operations.label: Synthesize second strand

operations.label: The forward-strand is cleaved and washed away

operations.information_effect: The first template is removed physically while its complementary sequence copy preserves the fragment relationship for the second read.

evidence.locator: Far right, The forward-strand is cleaved and washed away: faded departing strand, short surface remnant and retained full-length opposite-orientation strand

operations.label: The second read is sequenced

method_scopes.rationale: One title and one retained material route identify the scoped component illustration. All 17 local operations apply to this illustrated indexed paired-end route. The two Synthesize second strand captions and two The read product is washed away captions are separate local operations with different inputs/history. Index 2 uses the drawn P5 extension, and Read 2 uses the opposite strand made through that route. No alternative target workflow is explicitly depicted, and this scope does not generalize those preparations to all sequencing-by-synthesis implementations.

checks.rationale: Independent inspection supports this diagram-level architecture. All 17 local operations and their 49 connections preserve the drawn material histories: adapter capture, complementary copying, initial strand removal, repeated surface bridge amplification, reverse-strand removal, Read 1 and its removal, Index 1 and its removal, P5 turnaround with Index 2, completion of the opposite strand, forward-strand removal and Read 2. The 33 states distinguish persistent surface templates, departing physical products, nucleotide/primer inputs and inferred sequence data. Multi-input operations combine the depicted template with its relevant surface or incorporated substrates; multi-output operations represent one separation or one sequencing event and its physical/data outputs. Repeated captions are separate local instances, with no independent branches collapsed or invented pooling. The flowcell and fluorescent insets are explanatory magnifications. No consequential unsupported assertion, omitted transformation or contradictory interface remains. Biological provenance, exact end-group chemistry, cycling-reset chemistry and downstream analysis are unshown and are not required to complete this schematic. The supplied catalogue identifies the title only and lists no publications; empty paper_matches and corrections are appropriate, with no primary-paper verification implied.
